decision_perspective: Japanese wording of the complex-phase selfcheck family only

dispositions.referent: The unit-modulus complex part z/|z|, not the real argument angle
dispositions.reason: The supplied preceding definition explicitly extracts the normalized complex number. Japanese physics usage permits 位相 for this unit complex part; 位相は1 is therefore not a naming defect in this context.

comparison.alternatives_or_not_applicable: 位相因子 explicitly stresses the factor; 偏角 identifies the angle instead and would change the referent; フェーズ offers no recognition benefit.
comparison.audience_reason: Physics readers can retain the established 位相 with the supplied normalized-complex-number definition. No obligatory replacement with 位相因子 follows from variation in angle-versus-factor usage.

evidence_sources.usage: Tasaki explicitly distinguishes the real 偏角 theta from the unit complex exponential called 位相 (phase).
evidence_sources.genre: Physics-oriented mathematical textbook by its author

evidence_sources.locator: https://www2.yukawa.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~soken.editorial/sokendenshi/vol11/1/Netsuba2011Proc.pdf contribution on cumulant expansion, section 3, eq.6
evidence_sources.usage: 複素位相 is the exponential e^{i theta}; its expectation is discussed as a complex phase factor, rather than the expectation of the angle.

supplemental_concepts.surface: 確認：$n=1$ の主要項の位相は $1$ になるか
supplemental_concepts.reason: The complete summary is a question, not a new formal concept name. Its scientific handles 主要項 and 位相 receive separate occurrence-bound judgments below and above; 確認 and になるか are ordinary framing syntax.

supplemental_concepts.referent: The dominant retained term in the approximation already presented
supplemental_concepts.reason: 主要項 identifies the retained leading contribution rather than defining a novel named object. It is established Japanese wording for leading contributions in physical asymptotic approximations.

comparison.alternatives_or_not_applicable: 先頭項 can emphasize written order; leading term or リーディング項 adds no precision needed here; 主項 is a legitimate compressed variant.
comparison.audience_reason: 主要項 directly identifies the dominant contribution already calculated and is familiar in Japanese physical approximation prose.

evidence_sources.usage: The field factor is identified as part of the 主要項 of an ionization-rate asymptotic expansion.
An operator product asymptotic expansion is described as having 主要項 Op[fg].

supplemental_concepts.referent: The state expectation of the translation operator, the bra-ket quantity already defined in supplied context
supplemental_concepts.reason: 期待値 is the standard quantum-mechanical name; it is not an invented ordinary description for this operator quantity.

comparison.alternatives_or_not_applicable: 平均値 is a broader gloss; 期待値 retains the quantum operator convention; エクスペクテーションバリュー adds no clarity.
comparison.audience_reason: The familiar term links directly to the preceding bra-ket definition.

evidence_sources.usage: The state-vector expression <psi|O|psi> is called 演算子の期待値.
The notes use 期待値 for the operator/state expectation, including the transition to bra-ket notation.

supplemental_concepts.reason: Here であり predicates that this operation returns the degrees of freedom unchanged. The sentence does not introduce a formal operator name or replace a definition of 恒等演算子. 恒等操作 is intelligible operation-level prose; changing it to the formal name 恒等演算子 is not required by Japanese terminology.

一周 specifies the distance around the previously fixed cylinder circumference; 並進 describes the action already introduced as a displacement along y. The complete phrase is a concrete operation description, not a name for a new formal transformation. Naming uncertainty would be manufactured here.

scope_note: The full three-line packet was read. Other already-established scientific inputs (中心電荷, Gauss–Milgram 関係, 規格化した状態) are outside this single term-family perspective and receive no independent verdict here. Formula validity and pedagogical sufficiency are not judged.
verdict: PASS for the assigned complex-phase Japanese wording family only
